In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the nNO level is not a reliable marker of ciliary function and ciliary dyskineis in PCD.
the NOS2 isoform is involved in the regulation of nNO production, and that NOS3 expression correlates with ciliary morphology and function.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
nNO is an important factor in the regulation of the ciliary beating and that NOS isoforms are differently involved in the regulation of ciliary beating in PCD and SCD patients.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the nNO levels are higher in patients with PDC and NOS3 thyme 894 mutation, which may be due to the higher ciliary beat frequencies in these patients.
nNO levels may be used as a non-invasive test to assess ciliary function in children with PCD.
the NOS2 isoform seems to be the main source of NO in the nasal mucosa, and its expression correlates with nNO levels.
